question: Rain is liquid ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**precipitation**__.

__
 
• In meteorology, **precipitation** is any product of the condensation of atmospheric water vapor under the gravitational pull from clouds.

 
 
• **The main forms of precipitation include drizzle, rain, hail, snow, ice pellets, graupel, and hail**__.
 
• Precipitation occurs when a part of the atmosphere becomes saturated with water vapor (reaching 100% relative humidity), causing the water to condense and "precipitate" or fall off.
 
• Thus, fog and mist are not rain but colloid, because the water vapor is not condensed enough for precipitation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Condensation** is the process in which water vapor becomes liquid.

 
 
• This is the reverse of evaporation, where liquid water becomes vapor.
 
• Condensation occurs in one of two ways: either the air cools to its dew point or it becomes so saturated with water vapor that it cannot hold any more water.
 
 
 
• **Sedimentation **is a physical water treatment process in which gravity is used to remove suspended solids from water.
 
 
• Solid particles trapped in a moving water disturbance can be naturally removed by sedimentation in the still waters of lakes and oceans.
 
• For example, in a mixture of sand and water, sand settles down at the bottom.
 
 
 
• **Decantation** is a process for the separation of mixtures of immiscible liquids or of a liquid and a solid mixture such as a suspension. 
 
 
• Example: decantation of oil and vinegar.
